arxiv-2101-05158.title: UFL Dual Spaces, a proposal
arxiv-2101-05158.creator: David Ham
arxiv-2101-05158.description: Abstract This white paper highlights current limitations in the algebraic closure Unified Form Language (UFL). UFL currently represents forms over finite element spaces, however finite element problems naturally result in objects in the dual to a finite element space, and operators mapping between primal and dual finite element spaces.

arxiv-2111-12250.title: Analysis of Fröhlich bipolarons
arxiv-2111-12250.creator: Lisa Lin, Peter B. Littlewood, Alex Edelman
arxiv-2111-12250.description: Abstract Following a resurgence of interest in dilute superconductivity in polar semiconductors, we perform a variational calculation to probe the existence of Fröhlich bipolarons in these materials. Our solution is capable of interpolating between the weak- and strong-coupling limits of the electron-phonon interaction.

arxiv-2301-01699.title: Data-driven modelling of turbine wake interactions and flow resistance in large wind farms Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2301-01699.creator: Andrew Kirby*, François-Xavier Briol, Thomas D. Dunstan, Takafumi Nishino, Kirby A, Briol F-X, Dunstan T.D, Nishino T
arxiv-2301-01699.description: Abstract Turbine wake and local blockage effects are known to alter wind farm power production in two different ways: (1) by changing the wind speed locally in front of each turbine; and (2) by changing the overall flow resistance in the farm and thus the so-called farm blockage effect.

arxiv-2308-10814.title: Jumping through Local Minima: Quantization in the Loss Landscape of Vision Transformers
arxiv-2308-10814.creator: Natalia Frumkin Dibakar Gope Diana Marculescu
arxiv-2308-10814.description: Abstract Quantization scale and bit-width are the most important parameters when considering how to quantize a neural network. Prior work focuses on optimizing quantization scales in a global manner through gradient methods (gradient descent & Hessian analysis). Yet, when applying perturbations to quantization scales, we observe a very jagged, highly non-smooth test loss landscape.

arxiv-2309-11526.title: Likelihood-based Sensor Calibration using Affine Transformation This project was partly funded by the German Federal Ministry of Food and Agriculture (BMEL) projects ”KI-Pilot” under Grant 2820KI001, and ”PINOT” under Grant 28DK107G20, and the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate
arxiv-2309-11526.creator: Guido Dartmann, This work has been published by IEEE under DOI: 10.1109/JSEN.2023.3341503
arxiv-2309-11526.description: Abstract An important task in the field of sensor technology is the efficient implementation of adaptation procedures of measurements from one sensor to another sensor of identical design. One idea is to use the estimation of an affine transformation between different systems, which can be improved by the knowledge of experts.

arxiv-2310-02924.title: Quantum forgery attacks against OTR structures based on Simon’s algorithm
arxiv-2310-02924.creator: Wenjie Liu, Mengting Wang, Zixian Li
arxiv-2310-02924.description: Abstract Classical forgery attacks against Offset Two-round (OTR) structures require some harsh conditions, such as some plaintext and ciphertext pairs need to be known, and the success probability is not too high. To solve these problems, a quantum forgery attack on OTR structure using Simon’s algorithm is proposed.

arxiv-2403-18124.title: Stochastic Finite Volume Method for Uncertainty Management in Gas Pipeline Network Flows
arxiv-2403-18124.creator: Saif R. Kazi, Sidhant Misra, Svetlana Tokareva, Kaarthik Sundar, Anatoly Zlotnik
arxiv-2403-18124.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Saif R. Kazi, Sidhant Misra, Svetlana Tokareva, Kaarthik Sundar, Anatoly Zlotnik. Natural gas consumption by users of pipeline networks is subject to increasing uncertainty that originates from the intermittent nature of electric power loads serviced by gas-fired generators. To enable computationally efficient optimization of gas network flows subject to uncertainty, we develop a finite volume representation of stochastic solutions of hyperbolic partial differential equation (PDE) systems on graph-connected domains with nodal coupling and boundary conditions.

arxiv-2405-20338.title: Geometrical mixed finite element methods for fourth order obstacle problems in linearised elasticity
arxiv-2405-20338.creator: Paolo Piersanti, Tianyu Sun
arxiv-2405-20338.description: Abstract . This paper introduces a mixed Finite Element Method aimed at approximating solutions to fourth-order variational problems with constraints. We first address the biharmonic obstacle problem and propose an error convergence framework that offers an alternative to the established approaches by Ciarlet & Raviart and Ciarlet & Glowinski.

arxiv-2510-01206.title: Accelerating Long-Term Molecular Dynamics with Physics-Informed Time-Series Forecasting
arxiv-2510-01206.creator: Hung Le, Sherif Abbas, Minh Hoang Nguyen, Van Dai Do, Huu Hiep Nguyen, Dung Nguyen
arxiv-2510-01206.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hung Le, Sherif Abbas, Minh Hoang Nguyen, Van Dai Do, Huu Hiep Nguyen, Dung Nguyen. Efficient molecular dynamics (MD) simulation is vital for understanding atomic-scale processes in materials science and biophysics. Traditional density functional theory (DFT) methods are computationally expensive, which limits the feasibility of long-term simulations. We propose a novel approach that formulates MD simulation as a time-series forecasting problem, enabling advanced forecasting models to predict atomic trajectories via displacements rather than absolute positions.

arxiv-2510-03594.title: Variable Block-Correlation Modeling and Optimization for Secrecy Analysis in Fluid Antenna Systems Thanks: ( Corresponding author: Kai-Kit Wong. ) Thanks: This research work of T. Wu was funded by Hong Kong Research Grants Council under the Area of Excellence Scheme under Grant AoE/E-101/23-N. T. Wu
arxiv-2510-03594.creator: Tuo Wu, Kwai-Man Luk, Jie Tang, Kai-Kit Wong, Fellow, IEEE, Jianchao Zheng, Baiyang Liu
arxiv-2510-03594.description: Abstract Fluid antenna systems (FAS) are emerging as a transformative enabler for sixth-generation (6G) wireless communications, providing unprecedented spatial diversity through dynamic reconfiguration of antenna ports. However, the inherent spatial correlation among ports poses significant challenges for accurate analysis. Conventional models such as Jakes are analytically intractable, while oversimplified constant-correlation models fail to capture the true behavior.

pmc-11602927.title: Open-lung ventilation versus no ventilation during cardiopulmonary bypass in an innovative animal model of heart transplantation
pmc-11602927.creator: Varun Karnik, Sebastiano Maria Colombo, Leah Rickards, Silver Heinsar, Louise E See Hoe, Karin Wildi, Margaret R Passmore, Mahe Bouquet, Kei Sato, Carmen Ainola, Nicole Bartnikowski, Emily S Wilson, Kieran Hyslop, Kris Skeggs, Nchafatso G Obonyo, Charles McDonald, Samantha Livingstone, Gabriella Abb
pmc-11602927.description: Open-lung ventilation during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) in patients undergoing heart transplantation (HTx) is a potential strategy to mitigate postoperative acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). We utilized an ovine HTx model to investigate whether open-lung ventilation during CPB reduces postoperative lung damage and complications.

pmc-11659934.title: Pollinator functional group abundance and floral heterogeneity in an agroecological context affect mating patterns in a self‐incompatible wild plant
pmc-11659934.creator: Audrey Labonté, Valérie Le Corre, Annick Matejicek, Emeline Felten, Mélinda Turpin, Emilien Laurent, Séverine Michel, Chantal Ducourtieux, Eric Vieren, Willem Proesmans, Violaine Deytieux, Stéphane Cordeau, Adam J Vanbergen
pmc-11659934.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PremiseRestoration of seminatural field margins can elevate pollinator activity. However, how they support wild plant gene flow through interactions between pollinators and spatiotemporal gradients in floral resources remains largely unknown.MethodsUsing a farm‐scale experiment, we tested how mating outcomes (expected heterozygosity and paternity correlation) of the wild, self‐incompatible plant Cyanus segetum transplanted into field margins (sown wildflower or grass‐legume strips) were affected by the abundance of different pollinator functional groups (defined by species traits).

pmc-11710017.title: The neurophysiological effects of frontotemporal lobar degeneration: linking synaptic loss, network connectivity and cognitive decline
pmc-11710017.creator: James B Rowe
pmc-11710017.description: BackgroundFrontotemporal dementia (FTD) and Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP) have distinct molecular pathologies, with Tau and TDP43 aggregation, and distinct patterns of regional brain atrophy. However, they share the synaptotoxicity of protein aggregation, and neurotransmitter loss (including GABA), which contribute to clinical and neurophysiological similarities.

pmc-12604755.title: Clinical epidemiological characteristics and antibiotic sensitivity of Escherichia coli urinary tract infection
pmc-12604755.creator: Zhi Wen, Jiwei Jin, Yonghong Chen, Chengjuan Zhao, Chengchun Xu, Jun Liu, Binglei Ge, Mabel Aworh, Mabel Aworh, Mabel Aworh, Mabel Aworh, Mabel Aworh
pmc-12604755.description: IntroductionUrinary tract infections are common types of infections around the world, and most urinary tract infections are caused by Escherichia coli (E. coli). In order to better understand the clinical characteristics of E. coli in urinary tract infections and to guide empirical treatment, we conducted this study.MethodsE. coli in hospitalized patients with urinary tract infection in 2023 was retrospectively analyzed.

pmc-12639254.title: Urethral prolapse following female genital mutilation in a 9-year-old Somali girl: A rare case report
pmc-12639254.creator: Abdishakur Mohamed Abdi, Abdisalam Ismail Hassan, Abdirahman Ahmed Mohamud, Ismail Mohamoud Abdullahi, Mohamed Rage Ahmed, Ahmed Muhammad Bashir
pmc-12639254.description: Urethral prolapse (UP) is a rare benign condition, typically seen in prepubertal girls and postmenopausal women, with estrogen deficiency and raised intra-abdominal pressure as common factors. We report the first documented case of UP in a child following female genital mutilation (FGM). A 9-year-old Somali girl presented with painful genital swelling six months after undergoing type II FGM.
